To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the cross section of 7Be(p,gamma)8B reaction with the Coulomb dissociation technique at low energies and the extracted S17(0) factor is 18.9+/-1.8 e V-b.
we have measured the dissociations of 8B and 7Be in the Coulomb fields of 208P
the astrophysical S-factor for 7Be(p,gamma)8B reaction is determined to be 18(2) eV b at Erel = 0.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the 7Li(p,γ) 8Be reaction, which is the first step of the proton-proton chain in the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN), and the 7Be (p,γ) 7B reaction, which is one of the key reactions in the production of 8B solar neutrino.
the study of the reaction of 7Be(p,gamma)8B, which is of fundamental importance to the standard solar model.
the study of the 7 Be(p, γ)8 B reaction, which is the dominant reaction for the solar neutrinos production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S17 factor at zero energy is 18.9 eV-b with a 10% uncertainty, which is consistent with the value of 20.0±0.3 eV-b deduced from the solar-neutrino data.
the S factor at 0 eV has been measured by the present and previous Coulomb dissociation experiments with a precision of ±10% and the direct capture measurements with a precision of about 20%.
the astrophysical S factor of 7Be(p,gamma)8B reaction is S(0) = 18.9+/-1.8 e V-b, which implies a 7Be(p(gamma)8B solar-neu-trino production rate of 6.0 +/- 0.6 SNU.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 8B neutrino production rate is 5.8±1.0×106 yr−1, and the S factor at zero is 18.9+2.0−1.7 eV-b.
the astrophysical S factor at zero is 18.9 eV-b and that the 8B production rate in the sun is (6.0±0.5)×106 cm-3s-1.
the astrophysical S factor of the 7 Be(p,γ) 8B reaction is 18.9 ± 1.8 e V-b at Erel = 0, which is 2.5 ± 1.2 e V-b higher than the value of the standard solar model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 7Be solar neutrino flux is robust, as the 7Be p-capture cross section is well determined at the low energies of interest for the Sun.
the Coulomb dissociation method can be used for measuring cross sections of reactions with low cross sections, which are difficult to measure by the direct methods.
the S factors of 7Be(p,gamma)8B at zero and low energies have been well determined, and the 8B neutrino production rate has been reduced by a factor of 2.4 from our previous work.
